title: They Put A Rowing Machine Where My Bed Was
mood: happy for her and lost at the same time
subject: coming home to find your childhood bedroom turned into your mother's home gym
caption: Midwest emo in the twinkle style. Two clean electric guitars in an open alternate tuning playing interlocking tapped arpeggios, splashy drums with lots of crash and ride, a melodic bass moving under the guitars, bars that shift meter between sections, a trumpet line in the bridge. Bright and intricate with big dynamic swings between quiet tapped passages and loud full-band sections. Male voice, earnest and strained, half-shouted in the choruses and cracking on purpose. 140 BPM with shifting meters, F major. Happy for her and lost at the same time. No distortion wall, no synth, no autotune, no programmed drums, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - tapped clean guitars]

[Verse 1]
Came home for Christmas, opened my old door
Mum's turned it into a gym, there's a rowing machine
Exactly where my bed was, the dent's still in the carpet
She's very proud of it. She rows at six a.m.

[Pre-Chorus]
I said "that's great, Mum" and I meant it
I also sat on the rowing machine for an hour

[Chorus]
They put a rowing machine where my bed was
And I'm happy for her, I swear I'm happy for her
It's just strange to find out you were a room
And the room moved on before you did

[Verse 2]
The glow stars are still up on the ceiling
She couldn't reach them, so they stayed
I lay on the floor where the bed used to be
Fourteen stars, I counted, same as when I was eight

[Chorus]
They put a rowing machine where my bed was
And I'm happy for her, I swear I'm happy for her
It's just strange to find out you were a room
And the room moved on, and kept the stars for me

[Outro - guitars cut]
I rowed two thousand metres
Terrible time. She beat it.
[Song ends abruptly]
